subject: Normal force on flat plates at high incidence and low aspect ratio, for the body-flap plate model
in_code: ExosphereSimulation BodyFlapAerodynamics.NormalForceCoefficient: subsonic C_N = (pi/2) AR sin(a) cos(a) + 1.2 sin^2(a); modified Newtonian above Ma 1.5; smoothstep blend between

entries.source: Hoerner, Fluid-Dynamic Drag (1965), as quoted in Monash 17th AFMC paper 212

entries.quantity: low-AR rectangular plates, 0.5 <= AR <= 2, alpha <= 50 deg, Re about 7e4-1e5

entries.source: Torres & Mueller (2004) as tabulated in Aerospace 10(7):597 (2023)

entries.statement: C_N rises to a plateau for 30 < alpha < 70 deg, then falls slightly toward 90 deg (pitching plate, AR about 4)

starship_flap_regime.aspect_ratio: about 0.45 (V3 forward, 2.55 x 5.7 m) to about 0.33 (aft, 3.7 x 11.1 m) using span/length
starship_flap_regime.reynolds: about 1e7 to 1e8 on the flap length at terminal speed
starship_flap_regime.note: far above the Torres & Mueller range; use only for the shape of C_N(alpha), not magnitudes

implication_for_heading_authority: A plate's force component across the flow, C_N(alpha) cos(alpha), peaks near 45-55 deg of incidence. Exosphere's flaps sit at a 45 deg neutral with hinges parallel to the body axis, so their heading moment has zero slope at neutral. Measured on the Flight 15 bench, see MODEL_COMPARISON.md.
